humanities_role_explanation: Designed to evaluate graduate-level history knowledge and comprehension, targeting disciplinary competence rather than general-purpose reading comprehension.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: The benchmark uses text-only multiple-choice questions formatted in a four-option structure.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Evaluates the factual recall and historical knowledge of models using a four-choice multiple-choice QA format derived from structured historical data.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Specifically focused on global history and historical societies rather than a general multi-domain evaluation.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates seven models from the Gemini, OpenAI, and Llama families, including GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-3.1-8B.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates model performance using balanced accuracy.

summary: This paper introduces the History Seshat Test for LLMs (HiST-LLM), a benchmark constructed from the Seshat Global History Databank to evaluate models on expert graduate-level history knowledge. Covering 600 historical societies spanning the Neolithic period to the Industrial Revolution, the benchmark highlights performance disparities across different regions and historical eras.
key_findings: The evaluated LLMs achieved balanced accuracies ranging from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46% (GPT-4-Turbo), outperforming the 25% random baseline but remaining well below human-expert performance. The models demonstrated better performance on earlier historical periods, with regional biases leading to lower performance in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa.
facets_explanation: HiST-LLM is constructed from the Seshat Global History Databank, a pre-existing structured database of historical data reviewed and assembled by history experts and graduate research assistants. Answering the questions requires domain-specific factual knowledge of historical societies not present in the prompt stimulus. The evaluation uses a four-choice multiple-choice format with a single correct key, and the treatment of annotator disagreement is not addressed in the provided text.
results_explanation: The paper reports that 'GPT-4-Turbo' achieved the best performance with a balanced accuracy of '46%' ('ranging from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46% (GPT-4-Turbo)'). No quantified human baseline is reported, though the authors note that models fall 'short of expert comprehension'. Regional asymmetry is identified, with performance 'better for the Americas and lowest in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa for the more advanced models' on a 'four-choice format' benchmark.
